svg.aria-label: QBM-07 · ROS production, scavenging and redox buffering
svg.text: QBM-07 · ROS production, scavenging and redox buffering
The amplifier that makes the review's hypothesis testable — and the reason it cannot identify a mechanism on its own

g.title:
Complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: flavin_semiquinone, iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, iron_sulfur_2Fe2S, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H, 14N, 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT5G37510, AT5G08530, AT4G02580, AT5G11770 rationale: The FMN site forms a flavin semiquinone during turnover and is a known superoxide-producing leak site, and the Fe/S chain performs sequential one-electron transfers — both of the physical routes the radical-pair and hyperfine arguments require. No published experiment has applied a near-null field and measured plant complex I activity, so this is a hypothesis with a mechanism, not a result.
caveat: Electron transfer along the Fe/S chain is fast relative to plausible singlet-triplet mixing times, so a coherent radical-pair effect here is harder to argue than at the flavin. Treat the flavin and the cluster chain as separate hypotheses rather than one.

Plastid superoxide / H2O2 tier T2 (reported) quantum class: ros_leak_site AGI: AT4G25100, AT2G28190 Parmagnani2023: Reactive oxygen species production differed between geomagnetic and near-null field conditions in lima bean. [10.3390/ijms24032896] Parmagnani2022: Near-null magnetic field alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis. [10.3390/biom12121824] rationale: As in the mitochondrion, the amplifier rather than the mechanism: threshold behaviour converts a small change in electron branching into a signal.

Peroxisomal beta-oxidation tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: ros_leak_site rationale: Acyl-CoA oxidase is a flavoprotein that reduces O2 directly to H2O2 as part of its normal catalytic cycle — one of the few places in the cell where peroxide production is the intended chemistry rather than a leak. During germination that makes the peroxisome a major ROS source at exactly the stage the review argues matters most.
caveat: A flavin semiquinone is not well established in the acyl-CoA oxidase mechanism, and the enzyme's own catalase-rich compartment quenches the product quickly. Classed only as a ROS source, not as a radical-pair site.

Mitochondrial superoxide / H2O2 tier T2 (reported) quantum class: ros_leak_site AGI: AT3G10920 Parmagnani2022: Near-null magnetic field exposure alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis. [10.3390/biom12121824] Farooq2021: Reactive oxygen species and mitochondria jointly regulate seed germination, establishing the route from mitochondrial ROS to a developmental outcome. [10.3389/fpls.2021.781734] rationale: Not a magnetosensitive mechanism itself — it is the amplifier. A field effect too small to measure as a rate change can still register here, because ROS signalling is threshold-like.
Superoxide dismutases (CSD1/2, MSD1, FSD1) tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT1G08830, AT2G28190, AT3G10920, AT4G25100

Ascorbate peroxidase (APX1, APX2) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: heme_electron_carrier nuclei: 57Fe, 1H AGI: AT1G07890, AT3G09640 rationale: Catalysis proceeds through Compound I, an oxoferryl porphyrin pi-cation radical — a genuine protein-based radical intermediate, and one of the few in the redox network rather than the electron transport chains.
caveat: The porphyrin radical is strongly exchange-coupled to the ferryl iron and extremely short-lived. Structurally it is a radical; whether it could ever be a spin-correlated pair with a geomagnetically relevant lifetime is untested and doubtful.

Catalase (CAT1, CAT2, CAT3) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: heme_electron_carrier nuclei: 57Fe, 1H AGI: AT1G20630, AT4G35090, AT1G20620 rationale: Like ascorbate peroxidase, catalase cycles through a Compound I porphyrin radical. Its relevance here is positional: it is the enzyme standing between germination beta-oxidation and oxidative damage.
Peroxiredoxin / thioredoxin system (PRXIIF) tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT3G06050

Ascorbate-glutathione cycle (GR1, DHAR1, MDAR1) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: flavin_semiquinone nuclei: 1H, 14N AGI: AT3G24170, AT1G19570, AT3G52880 rationale: Glutathione reductase and monodehydroascorbate reductase are FAD enzymes, so the same flavin semiquinone chemistry applies here as at complex I and FNR. MDAR is notable for acting on a stable organic radical — monodehydroascorbate — as its actual substrate.
caveat: The monodehydroascorbate radical is free in solution rather than held in a protein pocket, so it has no correlated partner and tumbles freely. It is a radical, not a radical pair.
Ascorbate / glutathione / NAD(P)H pools tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context
NADPH / NADP+ tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context

ROS-responsive transcriptional programme tier T2 (verified) quantum class: structural_context Parmagnani2022: Transcriptomics and metabolomics of ROS modulation in near-null magnetic field-induced Arabidopsis: field reduction alters ROS-associated transcriptional and metabolic programmes. [10.3390/biom12121824] Zsigmond2008: Arabidopsis PPR40 connects abiotic stress responses to mitochondrial electron transport, establishing a route from respiratory state to stress signalling. [10.1104/pp.107.111260] rationale: This entity carries demonstrated near-null-field evidence but NO proposed quantum route, and is classed structural_context to say so explicitly. It is the amplifier's output: threshold-like signalling turns an upstream change too small to measure directly into a transcriptional response. That sensitivity is what makes it the best-evidenced node in the atlas and simultaneously a poor discriminator — it reports that something moved upstream, never what.

svg.text: A weak-field effect on an electron-transfer branching ratio may be far too small to measure as a rate change, but ROS signalling is threshold-like,
so the same small change can register as a transcriptional response. That is why the ROS-responsive programme is the best-evidenced node in
the whole atlas, and equally why it cannot identify a mechanism: an amplifier reports that something moved upstream, never what. The map
deliberately includes enzymes with no spin route at all — the peroxiredoxin/thioredoxin system is pure two-electron thiol chemistry with no radical
intermediate and no metal — so that "redox" is not read as a synonym for "magnetically addressable". The heme peroxidases do cycle through a
genuine porphyrin radical, but it is exchange-coupled to the ferryl iron and extremely short-lived, and that caveat travels with the annotation.
Derived from: Figure 3 panel C and Figure 5 of Porterfield & Barker, "Plant Responses to Near-Null Magnetic Fields" — expanded to the scavenging
network and bound to Arabidopsis loci. Node counts by evidence tier: T2=3, T3=5, T4=4. Schematic topology only — no quantitative value is
encoded in this base map; numbers appear only when measured data is projected onto it. roots, 7 timepoints (10 min, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 24 h, 48 h, 96
h). 4 of 8 identifier-bearing nodes received a series (50%); 4 nodes carry no gene identifier and cannot. multi-locus nodes aggregated by extreme
at each timepoint. 3 node(s) reverse direction during the course (PLASTID_ROS, SUPEROXIDE_DISMUTASES, CATALASE), which no single-contrast
overlay can show. Each node is tinted by its most extreme timepoint and carries a sparkline of the full trajectory: the colour says how far it moved,
the line says when. A node with no measurement is left unfilled, which is not the same as a measured zero.
